verdict.reason: All three claimed elements verified verbatim. docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:88-91 types `activeCursorPos` as only `{ blockId; offset }` (while the sibling `activeSelection` endpoints on lines 94-95 do carry `lineAffinity`), and the §4 prose at docs-presence.md:190-194 positively asserts "`activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field". That is false against the working tree: packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:21-28 declares `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` inside `activeCursorPos` (its own comment saying "typing it keeps the wire shape honest"), and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-2974 accepts the same field on the publish path. docs-presence.md is the canonical Docs presence design doc and its §1 is the wire-shape record for `DocsPresence` (§12, line 550, names packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts as the `DocsPresence` type file), so a presence-payload/data-model change must be folded into it; instead the doc omits the field and states the opposite, misleading the next reader about the caret presence payload. This is a design-doc-discipline fit violation (major), squarely in the design-fit lane, not a line-level correctness or style nit. Only the rendering half of the prose ("peer caret still resolves 'backward'") is accurate, consistent with packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:99 and :337; the wire-shape claim is not. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, the stale doc text is reachable, and nothing elsewhere guards or corrects it.

finding.summary: Presence payload shape changed but `docs-presence.md` (the canonical presence doc) is now contradicted and un-updated
finding.evidence: The diff extends the presence wire shape in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-30` (`activeSelection.anchor/focus` now carry `lineAffinity`). The canonical presence design doc still says the opposite: `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:188` — "For remote cursors, `lineAffinity` is not in the presence payload. Default to `'backward'` ... acceptable for peer display", its `DocsPresence` snippet at :93-95 still shows endpoints as `{ blockId, offset }`, and :381 states "Default `lineAffinity` is `'backward'`, matching peer cursor rendering". Per CONTRIBUTING, a data-model change must update the canonical subsystem doc; instead only `docs-local-caret-anchoring.md` (the Yorkie-anchoring doc) was touched, leaving two design docs in direct conflict about whether affinity is in presence.

verdict.reason: The canonical presence doc WAS updated in step with the wire-shape change, so the claimed omission/contradiction does not exist. docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:93-95 shows the DocsPresence snippet with `anchor`/`focus` as `{ blockId, offset, lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward' }`, exactly matching packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34 (and :88-91 covers activeCursorPos, matching users.ts:21-27). docs-presence.md:188-194 states "Selection endpoints now publish `lineAffinity` (it rides along on the `DocPosition`s in `activeSelection`)" — the opposite of the quoted "not in the presence payload"; the residual `'backward'` default there is explicitly scoped to the peer *caret*. docs-presence.md:384-386 closes the loop: "`lineAffinity` defaults to `'backward'` here, matching peer *caret* rendering ... Peer selection endpoints carry their own affinity instead (see above)." The reviewer states a grep of `lineAffinity` across docs/design came up empty, but that grep returns docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md with these three passages, so the finding's factual premise is wrong. The update was folded into the canonical subsystem doc (no parallel file), satisfying the CONTRIBUTING design-doc discipline the finding invokes.

finding.summary: Design doc (and the new `DocPosition` doc comment) record a default that the implementation does not use
finding.evidence: The doc paragraph added at docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:80-90 says "it is optional, so a position without one keeps the historical backward reading", and `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:204-206` repeats "a position that carries no affinity keeps the default backward reading". But `packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260` implements `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` — the shipped default for a selection *start* is forward, not backward, and the new test 'defaults an affinity-less start to the forward reading' asserts exactly that. The design doc therefore misrecords the data-model semantics it was updated to document; the task file itself calls this "a deliberate deviation from the issue's 'keep the backward default' wording" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:20-26), which never made it into the design doc.

verdict.reason: The finding rests on quoted text that is not in the repository. docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:80-94 does not say "a position without one keeps the historical backward reading"; it states "An endpoint that carries none is read from the side its range extends towards: `computeSelectionRects` defaults a range's start to 'forward' and its end to 'backward'… A standalone caret keeps the historical backward reading." packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:196-214 says the same ("a range's start defaults to 'forward' and its end to 'backward' … A standalone caret still reads 'backward'"), not the claimed blanket backward default. Both match the implementation at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261 (start ?? 'forward', end ?? 'backward') and 472-473 (interior blocks backward). The task file's "deliberate deviation" note (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26, 60-67) is in fact carried into the design doc, contradicting the finding's final claim. No doc/implementation mismatch exists.

finding.summary: Flipping the affinity-less start default to 'forward' is out-of-scope behavior change affecting every other `computeSelectionRects` caller
finding.evidence: The change's own scope statement lists "Changing the default affinity for endpoints that do not carry one" under **Out of scope** (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:63), yet selection.ts:260 changes the default for all callers. `computeSelectionRects` is not selection-only: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1620` (peer selections), :1640 (search highlights), :1659 (comment marker rects, whose output is cached for hit-testing via `commentMarkerRects`), :1676 (spell-error squiggles) and `text-box-editor.ts:560` all pass ranges built from bare `{ blockId, offset }`. The stated justification ("only removes an invisible zero-width rect") is asserted in the lessons file, not verified for these consumers, and the accompanying doc/comment claim the opposite default — so the requested behavior for wrap-boundary endpoints could have been achieved without touching the shared default.

verdict.reason: The finding's cited evidence is misquoted. docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:62-67 does NOT list "changing the default affinity for endpoints that do not carry one" as out of scope; the Out-of-scope bullet covers the standalone *caret* default and explicitly states the opposite of the finding: "(The default for an affinity-less selection **endpoint** did change — start reads forward, end backward; see the acceptance criterion above for why leaving the start backward would have left the reported bug in place.)" The change is in fact an explicit acceptance criterion (todo.md:18-26), which also discloses it as a deliberate, written-up deviation from the issue's "keep the backward default" wording. The second prong — that "the accompanying doc/comment claim the opposite default" — is also not present: docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:84-87 states the same forward-start/backward-end default and notes the caret keeps backward, and the in-code comment at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:255-261 matches the implementation at :260-261. The code change and the other computeSelectionRects call sites (editor.ts:1620 etc.) do exist, but under the design-fit/spec-conformance rubric the diff conforms to its stated acceptance criteria and scope; whether flipping the shared default is behaviorally safe for the search/comment/spell consumers is a correctness-lens question, not a scope-creep violation.
